title: Iterating on LLM apps at scale  Learnings from Discord: Ian Webster
talk_summary: Ian Webster describes how Discord shipped LLM products at scale by treating evals as simple, local, deterministic unit tests run on every PR, keeping prompts lean, and using existing observability (Datadog) rather than bespoke tooling. He also covers red-teaming with attacker/judge model loops and pre-deployment risk assessment.

takeaways.technique: Evals as fast local deterministic unit tests per component
takeaways.what_they_do: Break the LLM system into small pieces (moderation, tool triggering, summarization) and write tiny deterministic evals for each, run locally and on every PR, rather than one big end-to-end LLM-graded eval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the goal here is fast uh tiny evals that are ideally deterministic
takeaways.numbers: checking output begins with lowercase letter got 'more than 80% of the way there for like 1% of the work'

takeaways.technique: Cheap deterministic proxies for subjective qualities
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of an LLM grader for 'casual tone', they check a simple deterministic signal (output starts lowercase) that correlates with the desired behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what worked well for us is just you know checking that the the output begins with a lowercase letter

takeaways.technique: Resist prompt bloat; less is more
takeaways.what_they_do: After piling failure-mode special cases into prompts, they hit diminishing then negative returns and removed much of the prompt, letting the model reason.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we realize that less is more and uh removing a lot from The Prompt

takeaways.technique: Occasional stronger-model nudge to correct drift
takeaways.what_they_do: When weaker models drifted from their system prompt over long conversations, they randomly injected a stronger-model response to pull behavior back on track.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we would occasionally drop in a GPT 4 response um just literally randomly

takeaways.technique: Attacker/judge red-team loop for app-specific jailbreaks
takeaways.what_they_do: An attacker LLM sends adversarial inputs, a judge LLM guides rewording/euphemisms to bypass safeguards, exposing app-specific prompt-injection vectors introduced by their own prompt layers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have an attacker um LM that sends adversarial inputs and then you have a judge that guides it

takeaways.technique: Use existing observability, not bespoke LLM tooling
takeaways.what_they_do: They pushed LLM metrics and simple one-shot model-graded production evals into Datadog alongside product metrics rather than adopting a dedicated LLM observability product.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best observability tool is the one that you're using already
